summary:
We developed **PLUTON** (Polar Lunar Utilities, Topography & Orbital Navigator), an interactive mission-planning web application and astrodynamics decision suite designed for rapidly evaluating Lunar South Pole landing sites and launch schedules.

Unlike fragmented legacy tools, PLUTON fuses JPL DE441 Sun and Earth ephemerides—accounting for 3D lunar libration—with curvature-corrected $360^\circ$ LOLA topographic horizon ray-casting in real time. The platform models the finite $0.533^\circ$ solar disk for partial penumbral power generation, optimizes deployable solar mast heights, simulates battery survival across $-200^\circ\text{C}$ eclipses, and evaluates Direct-to-Earth and Lunar Gateway relay windows. Mission planners can compare candidate sites side-by-side, simulate launch delays using a 30-day viability carpet heatmap, and toggle between a technical engineering HUD and an interactive educator mode.

At the Lunar South Pole, grazing sunlight and Earth's orbital wobble mean minor location or schedule shifts can cause fatal power loss or communication blackouts—risks underscored by recent polar lander anomalies. PLUTON replaces days of manual data stitching with instantaneous Go/No-Go telemetry, accelerating agile mission planning while making lunar exploration accessible to students and the public.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

PLUTON (Polar Lunar Utilities, Topography & Orbital Navigator) is an integrated mission-planning web platform and astrodynamics analytics suite built to evaluate Lunar South Pole ($80^\circ\text{S}\text{–}90^\circ\text{S}$) landing sites and launch schedules in real time.

  • Topography-Coupled Ephemeris Engine: For any candidate coordinate or custom pin dropped on the lunar surface, PLUTON marches $360$ radial rays outward across Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) Digital Elevation Model (DEM) terrain profiles—applying planetary curvature drop ($\Delta h = d^2 / 2R_{\text{Moon}}$)—to generate a $360^\circ$ local horizon elevation mask $h(\theta)$. Simultaneously, it computes topocentric Azimuth and Elevation trajectories for the Sun and Earth (accounting for the Moon's $1.54^\circ$ axial tilt, $5.14^\circ$ orbital inclination, and 27.3-day 3D optical/physical libration).
  • Penumbral Solar Disk & Hardware Digital Twin: Rather than treating the Sun as an infinitely small point, PLUTON models the Sun's true $0.533^\circ$ apparent angular diameter to integrate partial penumbral sunlight as it grazes crater rims. It translates solar elevation into power output for vertical pole-mounted solar arrays vs. horizontal deck panels, simulates hourly Battery State-of-Charge (SoC) across cryogenic eclipses, and allows engineers to adjust deployable mast height ($0\text{ m} \to 25\text{ m}$) in real time.
  • Multi-Node Communication & Launch-Slip Trade-Off Studio: PLUTON tracks Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight clearance (including a $2^\circ$ RF multipath safety margin), models communication handoffs to the Lunar Gateway in Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) during terrain blackouts, and generates a 30-Day Launch-Slip Viability Carpet Heatmap alongside a Site A vs. Site B Split Comparator.
  • AI Site Certification & Guided Descent: A Stacking Machine Learning meta-ensemble (combining Random Forest, Extra Trees, Histogram Gradient Boosting, RBF-SVM, and a Multi-Layer Perceptron) paired with Shannon Entropy + TOPSIS multi-criteria ranking evaluates thousands of polar coordinates against NASA STD-7000 flight rules and simulates closed-loop powered descent trajectories.

2. Key Benefits

  • Unifies Fragmented Workflows into 60 FPS Interaction: Replaces days of manually exporting raw ASCII tables from JPL Horizons and cross-referencing GIS elevation cross-sections in QuickMap or Moon Trek with instantaneous, single-screen visual trade-offs.
  • Democratizes Restricted Analysis Tools: Makes solar elevation, line-of-sight ray-casting, and surface lighting simulation—capabilities currently gatekept behind restricted researcher accounts on portals like Moon Trek—openly accessible in a standard web browser.
  • Actionable Engineering Metrics Over Raw Angles: Converts abstract orbital angles into concrete mission survival metrics: exact countdown timers to next Sunset and Earthset, maximum continuous eclipse duration, battery freeze warnings, and watt-hour gains per meter of mast height.
  • Accessible Across Skill Levels: Offers a Mission Planner HUD (with JPL Horizons live API verification, flight-rule audits, and CSV/JSON exports) alongside an Educator & Public Explorer Mode with guided visual explanations.

3. Intended Impact

  • De-Risking Lunar South Pole Landings: Recent polar missions (such as IM-1, IM-2, and SLIM) demonstrated how minor off-target landings or steep crater shadows can starve solar panels of grazing sunlight and cut off Earth communications within hours. PLUTON enables mission teams to stress-test $3\sigma$ landing dispersion ellipses and pre-launch site retargeting before launch.
  • Agile Response to Launch Delays: Rocket scrubs and hardware delays are routine in spaceflight. PLUTON empowers NASA CLPS, Artemis, CSA, and commercial mission planners to evaluate $+3\text{d}$ to $+30\text{d}$ launch slips in seconds and identify slip-tolerant launch plateaus.
  • Bridging Science and Engineering Teams: Science teams target dark Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) for water ice, while engineering teams require sunlit ridges for power and comms. PLUTON quantifies the exact spatial sweet spots—such as Shackleton Connecting Ridge and Malapert Massif—that satisfy both constraints simultaneously.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Coding Languages: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5/CSS3, and GLSL (WebGL shaders).
  • Web Application & 3D Visualization Stack: Next.js (React), Three.js & React Three Fiber (3D South Pole DEM mesh and grazing shadow rendering), astronomy-engine (client-side VSOP87/selenographic ephemeris propagation), Tailwind CSS, and Lucide Icons.
  • Machine Learning, Astrodynamics & Data Science Stack: NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Scikit-Learn (StackingClassifier, RandomForest, ExtraTrees, HistGradientBoosting, SVC, MLPClassifier, LogisticRegression), Matplotlib, and Seaborn.
    • NASA JPL Horizons REST API (ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api using CENTER='coord@301' for DE441 topocentric ephemeris verification).
    • NASA LRO / LOLA Altimetry & LROC QuickMap (South Pole elevation, slope, roughness, and PSR reference datasets).
    • NASA Moon Trek OGC WMTS (South Pole stereographic basemap and hillshade tile layers).
    • Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Moon Exploration Data (LEAP Lunar Utility Rover parameters and Lunar Gateway NRHO relay profiles).
  • Development & Compute Environments: Antigravity IDE, Kaggle Cloud Notebook environment (for multi-algorithm training, cross-validation, and 9-panel telemetry dashboard generation), local developer workstation, and Git/GitHub.

5. How Our Project Is Creative

  • Finite Solar Disk Penumbral Ray-Casting: Most student and standard tools treat the Sun as a $0^\circ$ point source. Because the Sun moves almost horizontally along the South Pole horizon, it spends hours partially peeking over mountain ridges. PLUTON integrates the circular segment of the $0.533^\circ$ solar disk above local terrain to capture true partial-power twilight windows.
  • Hardware-in-the-Loop Mast & Array Optimizer: Instead of static map layers, PLUTON lets users physically resize a spacecraft's solar/antenna mast ($0\text{–}25\text{ m}$) and toggle between vertical cylindrical arrays and horizontal deck panels, watching the $360^\circ$ mountain horizon silhouette drop and power density jump in real time.
  • Interplanetary "Porkchop" Carpet Plots Applied to Surface Operations: Adapting deep-space trajectory carpet plots into a Launch Date vs. Mission Day Viability Heatmap, allowing teams to visually distinguish wide, safe launch plateaus from "knife-edge" dates where a 48-hour delay causes battery freeze.
  • Gateway NRHO Relay Rescue Visualization: Visually couples surface Earth-libration blackouts with overhead passes of the Lunar Gateway in its 9:2 Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit, highlighting international partner infrastructure (such as Canadarm3 / Gateway) as an active communications lifeline.

6. Factors Our Team Considered

  • Airless Lunar Optics: Unlike Earth, the Moon has no atmosphere to refract sunlight over the horizon or diffuse shadows; terrain masks act as razor-sharp geometric cutoffs.
  • Lunar Curvature Drop: Over $50\text{–}120\text{ km}$ sightlines to distant peaks like Malapert Massif, the Moon's small radius ($R = 1737.4\text{ km}$) drops distant mountains significantly below the local tangent plane, which must be subtracted during ray-casting.
  • 3D Earth Libration & Topocentric Parallax: Earth is close enough ($\sim 384,400\text{ km}$) that an observer's surface latitude/longitude shifts Earth's apparent elevation by up to $\sim 0.26^\circ$ (topocentric parallax) on top of its $\pm 6.68^\circ$ latitudinal wobble.
  • RF Multipath Clearance Margins: A radio link requires more than $0^\circ$ geometric clearance; PLUTON enforces a $\ge 2.0^\circ$ elevation margin above terrain ridges to prevent ground diffraction and signal degradation.
  • Cryogenic Survival & Terrain Hazards: Balanced solar/DTE duty cycles against landing safety thresholds (terrain slope $\le 8.5^\circ$, surface roughness limits, minimum $20\%$ battery reserve during $-200^\circ\text{C}$ eclipses, and proximity to PSR water-ice deposits).
